title: Ink in water

data.source: Stam (1959), who published the de Bruijn identity; Shannon (1948); cited from memory. Computed by quadrature.

prediction: For a single bell curve being blurred, the Fisher arc of the path is sqrt(2) times the entropy gained; for a two-humped mixture the ratio of rates leaves sqrt(2); and on CRR's own carrier the entropy does not change over a half-turn while the arc is pi. Coherence is not entropy gained.
baseline: de Bruijn's identity (Stam 1959) and the entropy power inequality (Shannon 1948; Stam 1959). Decoy: change in the logarithm of the variance.
relation: identical up to sqrt(2) on the Gaussian scale family; a different quantity elsewhere
claim_posed_by: this room; Phoenix does not make it
status_line: CRR here is: saying something de Bruijn's identity does not (an arc along a path of distributions); the two agree up to sqrt(2) for one bell curve being blurred, and on CRR's own carrier entropy does not move at all.
why: de Bruijn's identity ties the Fisher information of one density, about a shift, to the growth of its entropy under blurring. CRR's coherence (Phoenix BASE) is the Fisher-Rao length of a path through a family. For a single bell curve the two are the same up to sqrt(2). For a two-humped density the rates part company, and on the carrier R4 works with (status ASSUMPTION) the entropy is constant while the arc is pi. Phoenix does not claim coherence is entropy; R6 says of the surplus that it 'is not entropy'. The claim that is only partly true is one this room posed.
